definitions.explanation: In a manner that is fitting, correct, and well-suited to the situation. Used in formal and professional contexts to describe actions done the right way.

examples.japanese: {適切|てきせつ}に{対応|たいおう}してください。
データを{適切|てきせつ}に{管理|かんり}する{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.english: It is necessary to manage data properly.

examples.japanese: {問題|もんだい}が{起|お}きたときに{適切|てきせつ}に{判断|はんだん}できるかどうかが{重要|じゅうよう}だ。
examples.english: What matters is whether you can make appropriate judgments when problems arise.

notes:
The adverbial form of {適切|てきせつ} (appropriate, suitable), formed by adding に. Very common in business, official, and technical writing. It implies meeting a standard of correctness rather than just being "good enough."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {適切|てきせつ}に{対応|たいおう}する: to respond appropriately
- {適切|てきせつ}に{管理|かんり}する: to manage properly
- {適切|てきせつ}に{処理|しょり}する: to process/handle properly
- {適切|てきせつ}に{判断|はんだん}する: to judge appropriately

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {正|ただ}しく: correctly — focuses on factual accuracy; {適切|てきせつ}に emphasizes fitness for purpose
- {的確|てきかく}に: accurately, precisely — emphasizes hitting the mark; more about precision
- {適当|てきとう}に: appropriately / carelessly — ambiguous: can mean "suitably" or "halfheartedly" depending on context
